title: Dynamic backstop reservoir + tapered burst policy for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Introduce a ‘backstop reservoir’ capacity pool plus a tapered-burst policy that provides short-duration, prioritized burst capacity for Dedicated tenants while degrading gracefully and preserving isolation and predictable costs.
context: Current Dedicated reserved pools provide committed throughput and a set of hard burst rules. We frequently see short, high-intensity spikes that either cause unfair preemption or force large overprovisioning. Engineering has prototyped a lightweight global backstop pool that can be consumed by low-latency prioritized taps; product must define requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout constraints, and operator controls.
goals: Reduce customer-visible failed requests or rejects during short spikes (<30 minutes) by using a managed backstop reservoir
Provide a tapered burst algorithm so tenants receive reducing burst throughput over time, preventing runaway cost and preserving long-run fairness
Maintain predictable SLOs for committed tenants: 95th/99th latency and token cost impact bounded
Expose admin controls (headroom, decay curve, tenant gating) and console visibility for auditing and billing
non_goals: Replace long-term autoscaling or sustained capacity commits
Provide unlimited burst capacity or remove tenant-level quota/accounting
Change core runtime scheduling kernels as part of this scope (only orchestration and policy)
requirements: REQ-1: Backstop reservoir must be configurable per-region and support a total capacity and per-tenant cap (e.g., 10% of cluster, per-tenant max X rps)
REQ-2: Tapered burst policy must define a time-decay function (example default: linear decay over 15 minutes with configurable half-life) and configurable priority weights
REQ-3: When backstop is used, system must emit events: allocation_start, allocation_progress (per-minute), allocation_end, preemption_trigger
REQ-4: Billing must attribute tokens served from backstop to tenant with a distinct cost tag and support a configurable surcharge or credit usage accounting
REQ-5: Admin console must surface real-time usage, projected depletion time, and historical credit ledger for at least 30 days
REQ-6: Safety guardrails: soft-evict that steps down burst before hard preemption; obey tenant isolation classes and SLA tiers
REQ-7: Canaries: rollout supports 3-stage canary (5%, 25%, 100%) with rollback hooks exposed to ops
REQ-8: Telemetry: Verify tail latency (p99) impact < 1.5x for committed traffic and cost delta per 1M tokens when burst engaged
REQ-9: Runtime hooks: prewarm/kv-cache hints for load predicted by reservoir allocation to avoid cold start latencies
REQ-10: Operational APIs to drain/evict or manually credit/debit a tenant’s backstop usage
design_constraints: Prefer incremental changes to router/orchestrator to reduce risk; no kernel-level changes in scope
Must integrate with existing RBAC and audit logs used by Private deployments
Avoid global single points of failure: backstop must be zonal/replicated and degrade per-region
Cost accounting must be deterministic and visible to customers to avoid surprise bill shocks
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: End-to-end flow: A simulated tenant spike (3x baseline RPS for 12 minutes) should be covered by backstop for at least 80% of excess requests with committed traffic latency p99 increase <= 1.5x
AC-2: Tapered decay: Observed throughput allocation follows the configured decay curve within 10% variance over 15-minute window
AC-3: Console: Backstop usage, depletion ETA, and per-tenant ledger are available in the console and match API telemetry within 1%
AC-4: Billing: Tokens served from backstop include the backstop tag in logs and billing reports and reconcile with the ledger for test tenants
AC-5: Safety: Under a synthetic tenant that attempts sustained high load, soft-evict triggers and hard preemption only after configured grace (default 3 minutes) and respects tenant isolation class
AC-6: Canary: 5% canary passes system tests and chaos injection (simulated node loss) without violating committed tenant SLOs; rollback path demonstrated
AC-7: Observability: Dashboards show headroom, reservoir fill level, allocations per tenant, and an alert when projected depletion < 10 minutes
AC-8: Documentation & runbook: PRD-linked operator runbook published and ops team sign-off obtained
rollout_plan: Alpha internal testing in staging with synthetic workload generator (2 weeks)
Limited customer pilot: opt-in for 3 existing Dedicated customers (4 weeks)
Expanded pilot: enable for region-level custodial accounts with 10% traffic routing to backstop (2 weeks)
Full rollout with feature flag and 3-step gradual ramp to 100% across regions (control plane rollout window 6 weeks)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Backstop exhaustion leading to abrupt preemption — Mitigation: conservative default capacity + depletion alerts + automatic soft-fallback to lower-priority model variants
Risk: Unexpected cost exposure for customers — Mitigation: charge-tagging by default, pilot customers billed at 0 surcharge until ledger and console validated
Risk: Cross-tenant interference due to misconfiguration — Mitigation: per-tenant caps, isolation classes enforced, preflight validation checks
Risk: Increased tail latency for committed tenants — Mitigation: strict SLO gating in canary and telemetry thresholds that block rollout if violated
open_questions: Q1: Default decay function: linear vs exponential? (engineering preference leans exponential for faster throttling)
Q2: Billing model: fixed surcharge vs credit bucket deduction — prefer credits for pilot to simplify reconciliation
Q3: Backstop elasticity: should backstop be allowed to burst beyond configured % with ops approval?
Q4: Integration with Dedicated autoscaler: should reservoir consumption signal autoscaler to prewarm nodes?
notes: Prototype built by ENG team uses a token-leasing pattern with per-tenant soft quota enforced in the router
